CVE-2026-56740.title: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. Prior to 3.30 ...
CVE-2026-56740.description: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. Prior to 3.30.14, 4.0.16, and 4.2.1, the JLine3 Telnet server remote-telnet module does not limit the number of environment variables a client may inject via the Telnet NEW-ENVIRON option, and TelnetIO.readNEVariables() in TelnetIO.java:1127-1180 stores each variable pair in a HashMap held by ConnectionData, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to flood unique variable pairs before the terminating IAC SE byte and exhaust JVM heap memory with an OutOfMemoryError. This issue is fixed in versions 3.30.14, 4.0.16, and 4.2.1.

CVE-2026-56741.title: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. Prior to 3.30 ...
CVE-2026-56741.description: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. Prior to 3.30.14, 4.0.16, and 4.2.1, the JLine3 Telnet server remote-telnet module does not apply an upper bound to terminal dimensions received via the Telnet NAWS option, and TelnetIO.handleNAWS() in TelnetIO.java:856-879 reads client-supplied width and height as 16-bit unsigned integers and passes values such as 65535x65535 to setTerminalGeometry(), allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to repeatedly alternate values and trigger continuous expensive rendering work that causes CPU exhaustion and denial of service. This issue is fixed in versions 3.30.14, 4.0.16, and 4.2.1.

CVE-2026-77420.title: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. From 3.0.0 un ...
CVE-2026-77420.description: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. From 3.0.0 until 3.30.15 and 4.3.1, DefaultHistory.matchPatterns(String patterns, String line) in reader/src/main/java/org/jline/reader/impl/history/DefaultHistory.java converts the HISTORY_IGNORE configuration value into a Java regular expression while escaping only part of its syntax, allowing other regex metacharacters to reach the backtracking engine. An attacker who can control application or user configuration can supply a nested-quantifier expression that is reevaluated whenever a command is added to history, consuming excessive CPU and indefinitely blocking the reader thread. This issue is fixed in versions 3.30.15 and 4.3.1.

CVE-2026-77421.title: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. From 3.0.0 un ...
CVE-2026-77421.description: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. From 3.0.0 until 3.30.15 and 4.3.1, the JLine built-in nano editor's regex search mode passes a user-controlled search term from doSearch(String text) in builtins/src/main/java/org/jline/builtins/Nano.java to Java's backtracking regular expression engine without a timeout or backtracking bound. A nested-quantifier expression evaluated against non-matching buffer content can consume excessive CPU and indefinitely block the editor session thread, and remote multi-user deployments can lose a worker thread for each affected session. This issue is fixed in versions 3.30.15 and 4.3.1.

CVE-2026-77422.title: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. From 3.0.0 un ...
CVE-2026-77422.description: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. From 3.0.0 until 3.30.15 and 4.3.1, the JLine built-in grep command in builtins/src/main/java/org/jline/builtins/PosixCommands.java accepts a user-controlled regular expression in grep(...) and, unless line-regexp mode is used, automatically adds a dot-star prefix and suffix before compiling it with Java's backtracking regular expression engine. The wrapping expands the backtracking search space, so a short nested-quantifier expression evaluated against non-matching input can consume excessive CPU and indefinitely block a command worker, including in remotely exposed shell sessions. This issue is fixed in versions 3.30.15 and 4.3.1.

CVE-2026-77423.title: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. From 3.0.0 un ...
CVE-2026-77423.description: JLine is a Java library for handling console input. From 3.0.0 until 3.30.15 and 4.3.1, the JLine built-in less viewer passes user-controlled search and display-filter patterns from getPattern(boolean doDisplayPattern) in builtins/src/main/java/org/jline/builtins/Less.java directly to Java's backtracking regular expression engine and repeatedly applies them to file content. A nested-quantifier expression evaluated against non-matching lines can consume excessive CPU and indefinitely block the session thread, and repeated sessions in Telnet or SSH deployments can exhaust a bounded worker pool. This issue is fixed in versions 3.30.15 and 4.3.1.

GHSA-6r3w-6jpj-x5w6.title: Native Stack Buffer Overflow in Public INPUT_RECORD.memmove JNI Method (Windows)
GHSA-6r3w-6jpj-x5w6.description: ### Summary The JLine3 Windows native library exposes a public JNI method `INPUT_RECORD.memmove(INPUT_RECORD dest, long src, long size)` that copies an attacker-controlled number of bytes into a fixed-size stack-allocated `INPUT_RECORD` structure without any bounds check. This bypasses Java's memory safety guarantees and may lead to arbitrary native code execution in the context of the JVM process. ### Details The public Java declaration: ```java // Kernel32.java:513 public static native void memmove(INPUT_RECORD dest, long src, long size); ``` The native implementation: ```c // kernel32.c:817-825 JNIEXPORT void JNICALL INPUT_RECORD_NATIVE(memmove) (JNIEnv *env, jclass that, jobject arg0, jlong arg1, jlong arg2) { INPUT_RECORD _arg0, *lparg0=NULL; // stack-allocated: ~20 bytes if (arg0) if ((lparg0 = &_arg0) == NULL) goto fail; memmove((void *)lparg0, (const void *)(intptr_t)arg1, // src: caller-controlled address (size_t)arg2); // size: caller-controlled, unchecked fail: if (arg0 && lparg0) setINPUT_RECORDFields(env, arg0, lparg0); } ``` `_arg0` is a stack-allocated `INPUT_RECORD` whose size is `sizeof(INPUT_RECORD)`. The `size` argument (`arg2`) is passed directly to `memmove()` with no check that `size <= sizeof(INPUT_RECORD)`. Supplying `size = 4096` causes memmove to copy 4096 bytes into a ~20-byte stack slot, overwriting the stack frame and saved return address. The method is `public static native` and is accessible to any Java code that can import `org.jline.nativ.Kernel32.INPUT_RECORD`. No reflection, unsafe access, or privileged operation is required. This native code is compiled exclusively for Windows targets. Affected source locations: - `native/src/main/native/kernel32.c` lines 817-825 - `native/src/main/java/org/jline/nativ/Kernel32.java` line 513 ### PoC ```java // In a Java application on Windows with org.jline:jline-native on the classpath: Kernel32.INPUT_RECORD rec = new Kernel32.INPUT_RECORD(); Kernel32.INPUT_RECORD.memmove(rec, <valid_readable_address>, 4096L); // Stack corruption occurs in the native frame immediately. ``` A stack-canary-protected build raises a stack smash detected error. An unprotected build may silently overwrite the saved return address. ### Impact **Type**: Out-of-bounds Write / Potential Code Execution **Who is affected**: Any multi-tenant Java application running on Windows with `jline-native` on the classpath where untrusted code can call the public `INPUT_RECORD.memmove()` method (e.g., Groovy/scripting shells, plugin architectures, shared JVM services). Successful exploitation yields code execution at the privilege level of the JVM process, escaping Java's memory safety model. ### Credits This issue was identified by Michał Majchrowicz and Marcin Wyczechowski, members of the AFINE Team.

GHSA-6r3w-6jpj-x5w6.description: ### Summary The JLine3 Windows native library exposes a public JNI method `INPUT_RECORD.memmove(INPUT_RECORD dest, long src, long size)` that copies an attacker-controlled number of bytes into a fixed-size stack-allocated `INPUT_RECORD` structure without any bounds check. This bypasses Java's memory safety guarantees and may lead to arbitrary native code execution in the context of the JVM process. ### Details The public Java declaration: ```java // Kernel32.java:513 public static native void memmove(INPUT_RECORD dest, long src, long size); ``` The native implementation: ```c // kernel32.c:817-825 JNIEXPORT void JNICALL INPUT_RECORD_NATIVE(memmove) (JNIEnv *env, jclass that, jobject arg0, jlong arg1, jlong arg2) { INPUT_RECORD _arg0, *lparg0=NULL; // stack-allocated: ~20 bytes if (arg0) if ((lparg0 = &_arg0) == NULL) goto fail; memmove((void *)lparg0, (const void *)(intptr_t)arg1, // src: caller-controlled address (size_t)arg2); // size: caller-controlled, unchecked fail: if (arg0 && lparg0) setINPUT_RECORDFields(env, arg0, lparg0); } ``` `_arg0` is a stack-allocated `INPUT_RECORD` whose size is `sizeof(INPUT_RECORD)`. The `size` argument (`arg2`) is passed directly to `memmove()` with no check that `size <= sizeof(INPUT_RECORD)`. Supplying `size = 4096` causes memmove to copy 4096 bytes into a ~20-byte stack slot, overwriting the stack frame and saved return address. The method is `public static native` and is accessible to any Java code that can import `org.jline.nativ.Kernel32.INPUT_RECORD`. No reflection, unsafe access, or privileged operation is required. This native code is compiled exclusively for Windows targets. Affected source locations: - `native/src/main/native/kernel32.c` lines 817-825 - `native/src/main/java/org/jline/nativ/Kernel32.java` line 513 ### PoC ```java // In a Java application on Windows with org.jline:jline-native on the classpath: Kernel32.INPUT_RECORD rec = new Kernel32.INPUT_RECORD(); Kernel32.INPUT_RECORD.memmove(rec, <valid_readable_address>, 4096L); // Stack corruption occurs in the native frame immediately. ``` A stack-canary-protected build raises a stack smash detected error. An unprotected build may silently overwrite the saved return address. ### Impact **Type**: Out-of-bounds Write / Potential Code Execution **Who is affected**: Any multi-tenant Java application running on Windows with `jline-native` on the classpath where untrusted code can call the public `INPUT_RECORD.memmove()` method (e.g., Groovy/scripting shells, plugin architectures, shared JVM services). Successful exploitation yields code execution at the privilege level of the JVM process, escaping Java's memory safety model. ### Credits This issue was identified by Michał Majchrowicz and Marcin Wyczechowski, members of the AFINE Team.
